claims.text: Prochlorperazine: thiazides may accentuate its orthostatic hypotension;
claims.quote: Thiazide diuretics may accentuate the orthostatic hypotension that may occur with phenothiazines.

claims.text: it may counteract the antihypertensive effect of guanethidine and related drugs;
claims.quote: Antihypertensive effects of guanethidine and related compounds may be counteracted when phenothiazines are used concomitantly.

claims.text: with propranolol, plasma levels of both drugs rise.
claims.quote: Concomitant administration of propranolol with phenothiazines results in increased plasma levels of both drugs.

claims.text: Prochlorperazine overdose: don't induce emesis (a dystonic reaction of the head or neck could cause aspiration);
claims.quote: Do not attempt to induce emesis because a dystonic reaction of the head or neck may develop that could result in aspiration of vomitus.

claims.text: for hypotension, epinephrine is not recommended as a pressor, since phenothiazines may reverse its pressor action and lower BP further.
claims.quote: Other pressor agents, including epinephrine, are not recommended because phenothiazine derivatives may reverse the usual elevating action of these agents and cause a further lowering of blood pressure.
